name: Muse Spark
tagline: Meta's general multimodal model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Muse Spark is Meta's general-purpose model on the Meta Model API. Meta's models page lists muse-spark-1.3 as the version to use for new work.
how_it_helps: Use it to read documents and images, draft and summarise text, extract structured data, or plan a build, by calling the API with the OpenAI SDK.
pros: Listed by Meta as the model to start with for new projects.
Works with the OpenAI Python SDK by changing the base URL and key.
The API supports structured JSON output and tool calling, which Meta's workshop code uses with this model.
cons: Audio understanding is not fully supported on this version; use Muse Voice Transcribe or Spark 1.2 for audio.
Pricing and rate limits depend on your account tier and are not recorded here yet.
Access depends on your Meta account and region; confirm with a test call.

prompt_style.technique: State the task, give the input, and say the exact output format you want.
prompt_style.format: Plain-language instruction followed by the input; ask for JSON when you need structured output.
rules: Name the output format (for example JSON with named fields).
Say what to do when information is missing.
Keep one task per request.
prompt_style.example: Extract the order items from this voice-note transcript and return JSON with customer, items (name, quantity) and delivery_date. Use null for anything not mentioned.

best_for: Builders who need reading, writing, extraction or planning inside their own app.
not_for: Audio transcription (use Muse Voice Transcribe) or image generation (use Muse Image).
unknowns: Exact supported input types (check video and PDF support on the model page).
api_snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_MODEL_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1")
response = client.responses.create(model="muse-spark-1.3", input="Your prompt here")
print(response.output_text)

name: Muse Wonder
tagline: Meta's most capable model on the API, in preview.
summary: Muse Wonder is a preview model on the Meta Model API that Meta's models page presents as its most capable option, with adjustable reasoning effort.
how_it_helps: Use it for harder planning and coding tasks where a stronger model is worth the extra cost, once you have confirmed access.
pros: Presented by Meta as its most capable model on the API.
Reasoning effort can be adjusted per request.
Called through the same API and SDK as Muse Spark.
cons: Preview status: behaviour and availability may change.
Meta's models page lists it for the Standard tier only; confirm your access.
Pricing and rate limits are not recorded here yet.

prompt_style.technique: Give the goal, the constraints and the definition of done.
prompt_style.format: A short brief followed by the relevant code or files.
rules: State constraints first.
Ask for a plan before code on large tasks.
Say how you will check the result.
prompt_style.example: Review this function for bugs. List each problem with the line it affects, then give a corrected version and one test for each fix.

best_for: Complex planning and coding tasks in a project you are building.
not_for: Simple extraction or drafting, where Muse Spark is the better starting point.
unknowns: Preview end date or stability guarantees.
api_snippet:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(api_key="YOUR_MODEL_API_KEY", base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1")
response = client.responses.create(model="muse-wonder-1.0", input="Your prompt here")
print(response.output_text)

name: Muse Voice Transcribe
tagline: Speech-to-text model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Muse Voice Transcribe turns speech into text. Meta's materials describe uploading a whole recording in one request, and live transcription over a WebSocket.
how_it_helps: Use it to turn voice notes, interviews or calls into text before another model extracts or summarises the content.
pros: Transcribes a whole recording with a single HTTP request.
Also supports live transcription over a WebSocket, per Meta's cookbook.
Meta points to it for audio instead of Muse Spark 1.3.
cons: Language coverage, including Nigerian Pidgin and Yoruba, is not confirmed here; test with your own audio.
Output details such as timestamps and speaker labels need checking on the docs page.
Pricing and limits are not recorded here yet.

prompt_style.technique: No text prompt: send the audio file.
prompt_style.format: Audio file in, transcript text out.
rules: Use clear recordings with little background noise.
Send one speaker's note per file when you can.
Check the transcript before using it downstream.

best_for: Turning voice notes, interviews and calls into text for later processing.
not_for: Understanding or summarising audio directly; transcribe first, then use a text model.
unknowns: Exact endpoint and request format: copy the official example into api_snippet.
Pricing, file size and length limits.

name: SAM 3.1
tagline: Meta's segmentation model, available on the Meta Model API.
summary: SAM 3.1 finds and outlines objects in images. Meta's workshop code calls it through the Model API and gets box outputs back.
how_it_helps: Use it to locate objects or regions in a picture, for example to count items, crop them, or highlight them for review.
pros: Available through the same API and key as the Muse models.
Used in Meta's workshop code to locate regions in documents.
Listed in the hackathon guide as a model to build with.
cons: Pathwise's taxonomy has no segmentation job, so this card is mapped to edit_image.
Output format and prompt options need checking on the docs page.
Your key must have sam-3.1 enabled.

prompt_style.technique: Describe what to find in the image.
prompt_style.format: Image plus a short text description of the object or region.
rules: Name the object plainly.
Use clear images.
Check the returned regions before relying on them.
prompt_style.example: Find every product label in the attached photo.

best_for: Locating and outlining objects in images inside your own app.
not_for: Generating new images or describing a scene in prose.
unknowns: Exact request and response format: copy the official example into api_snippet.

name: Muse Image
tagline: Meta's image generation model on the Meta Model API.
summary: Muse Image generates images from text through the Meta Model API. Check the docs for editing options and output format.
how_it_helps: Use it to produce illustrations, product visuals or social graphics from a written description, inside your own app.
pros: Image generation through the same API key as the Muse models.
Listed by Meta among the models for this hackathon.
Model ID is published on Meta's models page.
cons: Output format and editing options are not recorded here; check the docs.
Region restrictions may apply; check Meta's Geographic Use Policy.
Pricing and limits are not recorded here yet.

rules: Name the subject first.
Add style and lighting.
State the aspect ratio if it matters.
prompt_style.example: A clean product photo of a handmade soap bar on a white background, soft side light, square format.

best_for: Generating visuals from text inside a product you are building.
not_for: Precise logos or text-heavy graphics that need exact lettering.
unknowns: Exact request and response format: copy the official example into api_snippet.

name: Muse Code
summary: Muse Code is Meta's coding agent that you run from a terminal inside a project folder. Meta's workshop used it to build an agent loop.
how_it_helps: Use it to plan and make code changes, run tests and report what changed, working inside the project folder you start it from.
pros: Meta's own coding agent, used in the hackathon workshop.
Signs in with a Meta Model API key.
Meta's cookbook lists bundled skills such as /plan and /taste.
cons: Needs macOS or Linux; Windows users need WSL.
Install steps are on Meta's docs page and must be followed exactly.
Cost of usage through an API key is not recorded here yet.

prompt_style.technique: Set ground rules first, then give one small task at a time.
prompt_style.format: A short instruction naming the files to touch and how to check the result.
rules: Ask it to inspect the repo before editing.
Give one task per prompt.
Ask for a report of files changed and tests run.
prompt_style.example: Inspect the project first. Add a Meta filter to the tools list, change only the files needed, run the tests and report what changed.

best_for: Developers who want an agent that edits a local project from the terminal.
not_for: Non-technical users who want a no-code builder.

name: Meta Model API
tagline: The API that serves Meta's Muse models and SAM.
summary: The Meta Model API serves Muse Spark, Muse Wonder, Muse Image, Muse Voice Transcribe and SAM 3.1. Its quickstart shows it working with the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs.
how_it_helps: Use it as the backend for AI features in your own app, calling Meta's models with an SDK you may already use.
pros: Compatible with the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs by changing the base URL.
Supports Responses, Chat Completions and Messages style calls.
Lists structured output and tool calling among its features.
cons: Availability depends on your account and region.
Model IDs and features change; check the models page before relying on a name.
Pricing and rate limits are not recorded here yet.

prompt_style.technique: Not applicable: this is a platform, not a prompt-driven tool.
prompt_style.format: Use the SDK with base_url set to https://api.meta.ai/v1.
rules: Keep your API key on the server.
Pick the model for the task.
Handle rate-limit errors.

best_for: Developers adding Meta models to an app.
not_for: People who want a finished app builder with no code.
unknowns: Full list of regions where it is available.

name: Muse Spark Open
tagline: Open-weight Muse Spark model you can run or access through partners.
summary: Muse Spark Open is an open-weight model from Meta. The hackathon guide says Baseten hosts it for participants under the name meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026.
how_it_helps: Use it when you want to run or host a model yourself, or use a partner endpoint, instead of the Meta Model API.
pros: Open weights, so you can run it yourself.
Baseten and Modal list support for Meta's open models in the hackathon guide.
Meta publishes an open-model cookbook for it.
cons: Capabilities and licence terms are not recorded here; read the model page.
You host it or use a partner; it is not served by the Meta Model API by default.
The hackathon model name differs from the name in Baseten's own docs.

prompt_style.technique: Same task-and-format style as Muse Spark; check the model page for details.
rules: State the output format.
One task per request.
Test on your host before relying on it.
prompt_style.example: Summarise the text below in five bullet points for a busy customer.

best_for: Builders who want to self-host or use a partner endpoint.
not_for: People who want the simplest hosted API path.

name: Muse Glimmer
tagline: Open-weight Meta model listed for the hackathon.
summary: Muse Glimmer is an open-weight model from Meta that the hackathon guide lists alongside Muse Spark Open. Most details still need to be checked on its model page.
how_it_helps: Use it if you want to run an open Meta model yourself. Read its model page first to confirm what it is good at.
pros: Open weights per the hackathon guide.
Listed by Meta among the models to build with.
Covered by Meta's open-model cookbook materials.
cons: What it is best at is not recorded here.
You host it yourself or use a partner.
Licence terms and hardware needs are not recorded here.

rules: Start with short, clear tasks.
Test before relying on it.
Compare with Muse Spark for your task.
prompt_style.example: Rewrite this paragraph in a friendly, simple tone.

best_for: Experimenters who want an open Meta model.
not_for: Anyone who needs documented, verified capabilities today.
